items.followUp: Explain how a vector is represented by a directed line segment, including what its length and arrowhead show.

rubric.why: A vector’s magnitude is represented by the length of its graphical line segment, using a suitable scale.
rubric.description: State that the line segment’s length represents the vector’s magnitude.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the length or scale of the segment to the vector’s magnitude.

rubric.why: The arrowhead shows the direction of the vector.
rubric.description: State that the arrowhead represents the vector’s direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the arrowhead as showing direction.

modelAnswer: Represent a vector by a directed line segment drawn to a suitable scale.
The length of the segment is proportional to the magnitude, and the arrowhead shows the direction.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and potential energy, and give one example of each.

rubric.why: Kinetic energy is associated with motion.
rubric.description: Define kinetic energy in terms of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that kinetic energy is energy due to motion.

rubric.why: Potential energy is associated with an object’s position or configuration.
rubric.description: Define potential energy in terms of position or configuration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that potential energy is stored energy due to position or configuration.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is energy due to motion.
Potential energy is stored energy due to position or configuration.

items.followUp: An engine receives 500 J of energy and gives 350 J of useful output energy. Find its efficiency as a percentage.

rubric.why: Efficiency is found from the ratio of useful output to input.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct energy or work ratio.

rubric.why: The output-to-input ratio is multiplied by 100 to express efficiency as a percentage.
rubric.description: Show that the ratio is multiplied by 100 or expressed as a percentage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including the percentage conversion.

modelAnswer: Alternatively, efficiency = (useful output work / input work) × 100%.

items.followUp: Define density and state the density of water in SI units.

rubric.why: Density is defined as mass divided by volume.
rubric.description: Define density as mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition or equivalent mass-to-volume expression.

rubric.why: The density of water is 1000 kg/m³, equivalent to 1 g/cm³.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either the SI value or its equivalent.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance: density = mass/volume.
The density of water is 1000 kg/m³ (or 1 g/cm³).

items.followUp: What happens to an elastic object when the deforming force is removed?

rubric.why: An elastic material recovers its original shape and size after deformation.
rubric.description: State that the object returns to its original shape or size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it regains its original shape or size.

rubric.why: The recovery occurs when the deforming force is removed.
rubric.description: Specify that recovery occurs after the force is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning removal of the force.

modelAnswer: Elasticity is the property of a material by which it regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.

items.followUp: A force of 20 N acts on an area of 0.5 m². Calculate the stress.

rubric.why: Stress is the applied force divided by the area over which it acts.
rubric.description: Define stress as force per unit area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition or equivalent expression.

rubric.why: The SI unit of stress is the pascal, equal to one newton per square metre.
rubric.description: Give the SI unit of stress.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for pascal (Pa) or N/m².

modelAnswer: Stress is the force acting per unit area: stress = force/area.
Its SI unit is the pascal (Pa), equivalent to N/m².
